description: Make the selected Ollama planner application-level local-only by validating the configured endpoint as loopback and scrubbing cloud credentials/base URLs from queued Aider subprocess environments while retaining explicit OpenAI behavior.
steps: In controller/main.py, keep PLANNER_PROVIDER as the explicit openai/ollama selector and normalize OLLAMA_API_BASE without query or fragment; accept only localhost or loopback IP forms used by the local server and reject non-local URLs before constructing the planner client.

Ensure the Ollama OpenAI-compatible client receives only the local /v1 base URL and the queued Aider command uses the Ollama model, with provider_environment removing inherited OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Google/Gemini credentials and base URLs and setting the validated Ollama base explicitly.
Preserve the OpenAI path and Generate's separate Anthropic path; do not alter generated-app files or broaden the feature into OS/firewall/network policy.
acceptance_criteria: PLANNER_PROVIDER=ollama with a public or non-loopback OLLAMA_API_BASE raises PlannerConfigurationError before a client or subprocess is created.
Loopback Ollama values produce a normalized local /v1 planner endpoint and ollama_chat model without requiring an OpenAI key.
The Ollama Aider environment contains the validated local Ollama base and none of the configured cloud credentials or cloud base URLs, while OpenAI mode still uses its selected key.
findings: Implemented and verified loopback-only Ollama endpoint normalization/rejection, URL-credential rejection, Ollama-compatible /v1 client configuration, expanded cloud credential/base URL scrubbing for queued Aider subprocesses, and explicit OpenAI separation. Verification from /Users/antoniociolino/voice-developer: controller/venv/bin/python -m unittest controller.test_planner_provider (12 tests, OK); controller/venv/bin/python -m py_compile controller/main.py controller/test_planner_provider.py (OK); git diff --check -- controller/main.py controller/test_planner_provider.py (no errors). Live non-destructive smoke used PLANNER_PROVIDER=ollama, OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen2.5:7b, OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:11434, and empty OPENAI_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_BASE; it reported provider Ollama / local-only, endpoint http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1, and response local planner smoke ok. lsof during the request showed the planner process connected to 127.0.0.1:11434; it also showed an established Ollama-process connection from 192.168.5.33 to 34.36.133.15:443, so the smoke observation does not prove OS-level no-network behavior and may include unrelated Ollama/background activity. Application-level enforcement is limited to this planner client and Aider subprocess environment; it cannot prove that other OS processes made no network connections. No generated-app files were edited and no cloud model was requested. Iteration 1 cross-FEAT verification reran controller/venv/bin/python -m unittest controller.test_planner_provider (15 tests, OK), controller/venv/bin/python -m py_compile controller/main.py controller/test_planner_provider.py (OK), and git diff --check -- controller/main.py controller/test_planner_provider.py (no errors). The no-cloud environment test passed with the expanded credential/base URL list. The loopback-only smoke used env -u for OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, Google, and Gemini credentials/base URLs and lsof observed only 127.0.0.1:11434 for planner PID 13964. This is application-level evidence, not OS-level proof that unrelated processes made no network connections or a firewall/router guarantee.
